claims: An appendectomy is the surgical removal of the appendix.
Appendectomy is typically performed to treat acute appendicitis.
Appendectomy is most commonly done via laparoscopy.
Laparoscopy for appendectomy uses 1–4 small incisions.
Laparoscopy for appendectomy uses a camera.
Laparoscopy for appendectomy uses gas to inflate the abdomen for better visibility.
Open surgery is used for more complex cases of appendectomy.
Laparoscopic appendectomy is the preferred method.
Appendectomy is performed under general anesthesia.
Appendectomy typically takes 30 to 60 minutes for uncomplicated cases.
Most patients return to normal activities in 1–3 weeks after appendectomy.
Full recovery from appendectomy takes about 4–6 weeks.
Risks of appendectomy include injury to other organs.
If the appendix bursts before surgery, the abdomen will be cleaned out to treat infection.
Patients often go home within 1–2 days after appendectomy.
An IV line will be started in preparation for appendectomy
